beats.t: Yeongnyangi slipped silently out of the sleeping room. Before closing the door, he looked back once. Yeoni slept with their mouth open, having kicked away the blanket.
Keep your blanket on. Catch a cold, and you'll blame Customer Support again.
He caught the blanket's edge with his paw and pulled it up to Yeoni's shoulders. Turning in their sleep, Yeoni hugged that paw like a pillow.
Let go. I'm not a pillow.
Yeoni did not let go. Yeongnyangi lay there for a long time, then very slowly freed his paw. He slid a book into its place.
Sorry. That book is Customer Support for today.
There was no answer. Instead, Yeoni mumbled one star in their sleep. Yeongnyangi smiled very faintly.
Climbing the stairs, he leaned a shoulder against the wall. His left paw refused to obey again.
He lifted it to look. Red rust spread over the scorch marks. Since his plunge into the water, it had grown one finger joint a day.
Scorched by fire, rusted by water. Iron needs quite a lot of care, too.
He covered the rust with his cloak. So Yeoni wouldn't see it tomorrow morning, either. Moka and Yundal had already noticed, but both could keep a secret.
No, the otter couldn't. That tail had probably told everything this afternoon.
The smell of rain drifted through the stairwell window. Whenever he caught it, something in Yeongnyangi's mind rattled open, then shut.
A bus stop in the rain. Water falling in strings from an old roof.
Someone's hand held an umbrella. A small hand. The umbrella tilted halfway toward the person beside it.
Beneath it, someone laughed. In the rain, like a fool, utterly happy.
Let's share. Someone said it in his memory. Yeongnyangi tried to catch the voice, but only rainwater filled his grasp.
He pressed his forehead to the cold wall. The memory always ended there. The hand holding the umbrella. Whose hand it was, who stood beside it.
If only I knew the name.
[ Contract, Article 1 · The guardian may not speak his own name · The moment the name is called, the contract ends ]
Golden letters appeared before his eyes, then vanished. Customer Support's rules. The rules he had personally signed when he first took the job.
I know. I've never forgotten.
He had forgotten what his name was. But he had not forgotten what he had agreed to gain by giving it up.
Just once more. This time, by your side until the end.
He looked at his reflection in the stairwell window. Navy hat, violet eyes spreading into gold, rusted paw. The face of a cat in a hat.
When I first opened my eyes with this face, you looked at me and asked if I was just a cat.
And gave him a star rating. One. Yeongnyangi still remembered that one star exactly, though he could not remember his own name.
The wind was strong on the roof. A half-eaten sun hung in the night sky. A sky that was neither day nor night.
The black tiger sat at the roof's edge, as though it had been waiting for him all along.
You're late, cat.
I smelled rain and came to look. Whose book are you here to steal this time?
I'm not here to work today. I have something to tell you.
No politeness for the pig, none for me. Who do you speak politely to?
Don't ask pointless questions.
The ledger's owner? That voice?
Shut up. That voice is listening even now.
The tiger glanced at the sky. The black half of the eaten sun writhed very slowly.
Its red eyes lowered to Yeongnyangi's left paw, finding the rust hidden beneath his cloak precisely.
That paw. Spreading a joint a day, isn't it?
How do you know?
It's all in the ledger. Every time you're hurt beside that child, the child's column grows heavier by a line.
Keep your paws off that column.
I'm not the one touching it. You are. The stronger that child's fire grows, the more you melt. And the longer you hold on, the smaller that child becomes.
Yeongnyangi said nothing. They both knew he had no answer.
Leave. Leave now, and that child can live with seven slots.
Seven slots make a vessel. You know that, too.
How do you know about that?
I can't read the ledger, but I can read the sky. Enough to know what that eaten sun wants.
Raindrops began falling between them. The sky was clear, but rain fell only where they stood.
And your rain. I think I've smelled it before.
You're imagining it.
An umbrella. A bus stop. An offer to share.
The tiger's tail struck the roof hard. Rainwater splashed upward.
Don't talk about that. You have no right to speak of that spring.
Then I was right.
We came from the same spring.
The tiger did not answer. Instead, it raised a paw and gripped the ring at its neck. Though the ring had done nothing.
Don't pretend to know when you can't remember. That's the cruelest thing of all.
I can't remember. That's why I'm asking.
I remember everything. Every last thing. That's why I live like this.
What happened that spring?
The person you said you'd protect disappeared. That's all.
Yeongnyangi's paw twitched. The rusted area suddenly burned. He had no memory, yet his body hurt before his mind could.
I see. That must be why I took this job this time.
It'll end the same way again. You'll be late again, and I'll be left alone again.
Don't ask. Why should I answer a cat who doesn't even know his name?
We're even, then. I don't know yours, either.
The wind blew. Deep in Yeongnyangi's eyes, gold flashed and vanished. A light that came without his knowing.
Those eyes just now.
Ignore it.
They were like that before the empty slot, too. Do you not know yourself, or are you pretending not to?
Customer Support does not answer personal questions.
Then a window opened below. Very carefully, but a little noisily, as a pig would.
The white cat and the black tiger turned at the same moment. A pink hoof hooked over the window frame.
